year.label: 2016 Cayman GT4 Clubsport with the Manthey MR kit

identity.real_world_identity_notes:
Customer racing Cayman GT4 Clubsport of the 981 generation, model year 2016, with the Manthey Racing MR kit. Curated first as the 2019 718 Clubsport of the 982 generation, which was wrong: the Extended Car Info spreadsheet this record was imported from carried the wrong year, and its author has since corrected it, noting that AMS2's interior matches the previous version. The simulator said so all along - AMS2 names the car "Porsche Cayman GT4 Clubsport MR" without the "718" that marks the 982. Assetto Corsa EVO's 718 Clubsport is that later car and wants its own record rather than a second entry here.

The MR kit leaves the powertrain alone, and the basis for saying so is the series regulations rather than a Manthey statement: Porsche Sprint Challenge gives the base 981 Clubsport MY2016 and the 981 Clubsport MR MY2016 one shared engine and one shared six-speed PDK with identical ratios. Manthey's own kit list adds suspension, aerodynamics, bodywork, fuel system, electronics and safety equipment, and includes no engine or gearbox modification.

wheel_rim.notes: A continuous conventional rim flattened at the bottom and closed over the top, with conventional spokes and a few buttons: d-shaped in this project's vocabulary. It is not a control-panel rim - there is no control face spanning two dedicated hand grips - and flattening alone never makes a rim gt-formula. Read from the complete dashboard photograph on page 88 of the MR's homologation dossier, which is this exact car including the kit's added wheel controls. Porsche's motorsport display elements are in the dashboard cluster rather than on the rim.

notes: Simulator behavior was directly observed in a guided drive with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.

AMS2 1.6.9.91 nonetheless required clutch input to move off. That is recorded as an explicit simulator override, so the in-sim guidance tells the driver to use the clutch while the record keeps the real car's value.
No throttle lift is required on upshifts and no manual blip on downshifts, because the drive detected automatic cut and automatic blip.

The real-car fields were withdrawn when the generation error was found and are restored here on 981 evidence. They came back to the same values - six-speed dual clutch, no clutch pedal - because both generations use a six-speed PDK, which is exactly why the error survived so long. The record now rests on sources about the car AMS2 models rather than on a coincidence.

AMS2 requires clutch input to move off, which the real car cannot: its clutches are worked by the gearbox control unit and there is no third pedal. That is a genuine simulator departure and stays recorded as an override.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.porsche-cayman-gt4-clubsport-mr.20260813t171028562z-e4f6b4a0 by Jason Kinslow.

overrides.condition: AMS2 1.6.9.91 requires clutch input to move off. Recorded so the driver is told to use the clutch in this simulator while the real car's requirement stays unknown; it previously read as a deviation from a clutch-pedal-free PDK, which was the 982's specification rather than this car's.

confidence.basis: Directly observed in the guided drive with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.
Simulator behavior was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is established by a registered manufacturer source.

claims.basis: The spreadsheet author's own correction establishes that AMS2 models the 2016 Clubsport of the 981 generation, and the exact simulator identity was observed live. Short of verified because the correction is a forum post rather than manufacturer material, and no 981 source has been reviewed for this record yet. Falsified by Reiza or Coanda stating a different model year, or by 981 material that does not match the modelled car.

Six paddle-selected gears on a sequential gate were counted directly in the guided drive. Porsche's and Manthey's material previously supported this and has been removed: both describe the 982, which is not the car AMS2 models. The gearbox construction rested on them alone and is now unknown; the gear count and actuation did not, because the drive saw them.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.
The guided drive established that AMS2 requires clutch input to move off, which differs from the real car's clutch-pedal-free PDK.

Porsche's vehicle description for the 981 Clubsport, model year 2016, specifies a "Rigidly mounted six-speed PDK-gearbox (DCT, dual clutch transmission)" on page 2, and the launch release independently describes a modified six-speed double-clutch transmission with steering-wheel paddles. The Sprint Challenge regulations carry the MR under the same power-transmission heading as the base car on page 47 with identical ratios, which is what extends the specification to this car rather than an assumption that the kit changes nothing. The guided drive counted six paddle-selected gears. Falsified by 981 material specifying a different gearbox, or by regulations separating the MR from the base car.

The MR's homologation dossier records "Clutch control system: GEARBOX CONTROL UNIT" on page 59 and a hydraulically actuated, normally-open dual clutch, so the clutches are worked by the gearbox ECU rather than by a driver, and a contemporary Road & Track first drive describes the car as running "without a third pedal". Short of verified because no manufacturer source states the absence of a clutch pedal or documents a standing-start procedure: the direct statement is a road test. Falsified by Porsche or Manthey material showing a clutch pedal in the footwell or describing a clutch-operated start.

The complete dashboard photograph on page 88 of the MR's homologation dossier shows the whole steering-wheel face: a continuous conventional rim, visibly flattened at the bottom and closed over the top, with conventional spokes rather than a control face spanning two hand grips. That is d-shaped, and the AMS2 cockpit agrees. Short of verified because it is read from a photograph rather than stated in prose. Falsified by a clearer view of the same car showing molded grips and a control face, which would make it gt-formula.

Neither is visible on the wheel face in the homologation photograph, and Porsche's vehicle description places the GT4 instrument cluster's motorsport display elements in the dashboard rather than on the rim. The AMS2 cockpit shows the same. Held at medium because this is an absence in a photograph: no reviewed source writes that the wheel carries no display or shift lights, and the MR kit does add controls to the wheel, so a later specification could differ. Falsified by a photograph or parts list showing a wheel-mounted display or shift-light array on this car.

deviations.basis: Six forward gears where the archetype has seven. The construction is the archetype's - Porsche's own vehicle description for the 981 Clubsport specifies a six-speed PDK dual clutch - and no six-speed dual-clutch archetype is registered, so this deviates on the gear count rather than crossing to a sequential archetype that would misdescribe the gearbox. That is the settled preference: a gear-count deviation over a technique or construction one.

Whether the car needs a throttle lift on upshifts is not established. The AMS2 drive predates the two-stage upshift test, so it recorded that a clutchless upshift worked without recording whether full throttle was refused first. A re-drive on the current client settles it, and the Assetto Corsa EVO drive of the 718 already answers it for that car.

driver_summary: GT4 racer using the road car's dual-clutch gearbox. It cuts the upshift and blips the downshift, and pulls away without a clutch, so the paddles and two pedals are the whole job.
